entry.title: From 404|1003 to the Green Lock: How I Fixed My Rust SMS Proxy on GCP with Caddy
entry.summary: TL;DR: I was calling my Rust SMS proxy on a Google Cloud VM by IP:8080, which caused Cloudflare 1003 errors and browser warnings. I mapped a hostname (example-proxy.example.com) to the VM, opened ports 80/443, put Caddy in front of my Rust app, and let it auto-issue a Let’s Encrypt certificate. Result: clean HTTPS endpoint that “just works,” and an easy env var for my Cloudflare Worker: SMS_API_URL=https://example-proxy.example.com/sms/send. I built a Rust program that proxies SMS requests. It ran fine at http://203.0.113.45:8080, but when I integrated it with a Cloudflare Worker and the frontend, I started seeing: 404 Not Found (from my origin on routes I hadn’t defined yet) Cloudflare 1003 (when requests were made by IP instead of a hostname) This post documents what the errors actually …
